title: bash gate reads no file verb behind find -exec, xargs, sudo or env
detail: Left out of v0.238.0. find -exec rm {} + and xargs rm name no file, and sudo or env put the verb past command position, so _FILE_VERB_RE skips them. xargs sed -i fails closed through $(stdin), but xargs rm stays unread. The corpus holds 124 find -exec rm targets, nearly all cache cleanup, so failing closed needs the find root and -name read first, or the gate's own cache cleanup gets refused.

thread.body: From gate-reads-commands (0.238.4): _named_commands now serves deny_commands and the lease, and the same wrappers hide a command from it, so this finding covers them too. command, time, exec, nohup, env, sudo, xargs and find -exec all pass a phase deny of git push. Read wrappers in _command_starts or _prefix_end so the write check and _named_commands both gain them.
